primary.controls: island fixed effects + year fixed effects + log1p island breeding-pair total

largest_colony_share.interpretation: The signal is not reproduced by dominance of the single largest colony alone.

ecological_interpretation: As Palmer Adelie breeders become distributed across fewer effective colony-code components, island-level chick production is lower than expected from the current number of breeding pairs, persistent island differences, and shared annual conditions. This argues against a simple retreat-to-the-best-sites interpretation of demographic concentration. The reproductive association is tied to erosion of the distributed breeding network rather than merely to the share held by the single largest colony.
mechanistic_boundary: The result does not by itself identify snow, predation, food limitation, density dependence or an Allee effect. Fine-scale snow/terrain effects on Palmer sub-colony persistence are already established by Cimino et al. 2025; the new result concerns the reproductive consequence of island-level demographic reorganization.
paper_implication: The Palmer story can now be written as a sequence: shared regional decline -> non-proportional within-island concentration -> size-ordered zero crossing that is mechanically expected -> reduced reproductive output as the breeding network contracts. Static island architecture need not predict this process across Antarctica, explaining why the original Paper 2 macro-architecture effect was weak and scale dependent.
